meta.status: ORGANISATIONS REAL, CONTACT ROUTES CHECKED ON 2026-09-22
meta.explanation: Every entry now carries verified:true and records in verified_by what was read and where. The honest limit on that check: the details were read in the organisations' own published pages as those pages were returned to us, because the network policy of the machine this was checked on refused a direct connection to the sites. No number has been dialled. A wrong phone number given to someone who is afraid to call at all is worse than no number, so re-check before each demo: set verified back to false and the '(check the website...)' suffix returns automatically on that entry.
meta.ordering_principle: Confidential advice is always listed before enforcement. A worker whose employer also controls their housing has a well-founded fear of retaliation, so the tool never leads with a body that may contact the employer. Enforcement appears lower down, and only as the user's own choice.
meta.language_claims: The languages array is what the organisation itself publishes as a contact route in that language - a phone line, a report form, or advice given in that language. It is not a claim that every caller is answered in it.

contacts.name: FNV (Federatie Nederlandse Vakbeweging)
contacts.what_they_do: The largest Dutch trade union. Advises workers on contracts, pay and deductions, including migrant workers, and can take a case up on your behalf. It runs a separate service for international workers and campaigns specifically on wage deductions for housing.
contacts.will_employer_find_out: No, not unless you ask them to act. Talking to a union is confidential, and your employer is not told that you contacted them.
contacts.typical_response_time: Days. Faster if you are a member, but they also answer questions from non-members.
contacts.contact: 088 - 368 0368, weekdays 08:30-17:30. For international workers: fnv.nl/migrantworker, or email migranten@fnv.nl
contacts.verified_by: FNV's service pages give 088-368 0368 as the Contactcentrum number, reachable every weekday from 08:30 to 17:30; the same number is printed on FNV's own letterhead in its published position paper on labour migration. FNV runs a hub for international workers at fnv.nl/migrantworker with migranten@fnv.nl as the email route, and publishes both Polish-language meetings for Polish workers and Polish-language chat support, which is what the 'pl' claim rests on. English rests on the international-workers hub being published in English.

contacts.name: FairWork
contacts.what_they_do: A Dutch NGO working specifically on labour exploitation and trafficking. They speak to workers in their own language, advise on what your options are, and do not require you to report anything to anyone.
contacts.will_employer_find_out: No. They work confidentially and will not contact your employer without your agreement.
contacts.contact: 020 - 760 0809 or info@fairwork.nu. fairwork.nu/en/contact lists a separate phone number and email per language
contacts.verified_by: 020 760 0809 and info@fairwork.nu appear on FairWork's own contact page and are repeated, with the address Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 32, 1012 RZ Amsterdam, in two independent directories (a social-services directory and a business register), which is why the number is written out here rather than only referred to. FairWork's contact page publishes a phone number and email per language and names Polish, Hungarian, Romanian, Bulgarian and Ukrainian alongside Dutch and English; Spanish and Portuguese are also listed but are not languages this tool offers.

contacts.name: Het Juridisch Loket
contacts.what_they_do: Free legal advice desk funded by the Dutch government. They will read a contract with you and explain what it means. They do not represent you in court but will tell you where you stand and refer you on.
contacts.will_employer_find_out: No. This is advice to you, and they do not contact your employer.
contacts.typical_response_time: Same week; they make a call-back appointment, and the offices have walk-in hours.
contacts.contact: 0800 - 8020, free, Monday to Friday 09:00-17:00. juridischloket.nl/contact lists the walk-in offices
contacts.verified_by: The free number is 0800-8020, Monday to Friday 09:00-17:00, on Het Juridisch Loket's own contact and location pages. Worth recording because it is exactly the failure this file exists to prevent: the number widely repeated elsewhere is the old paid 0900-8020 line at 25 cents a minute. English rests on juridischloket.nl/en, the organisation's own English site.

contacts.name: Stichting Barka (Barka Foundation Netherlands)
contacts.what_they_do: Supports Central and Eastern European migrants in the Netherlands in their own language, with mobile teams in several cities. Their focus is people whose situation has already broken down - work and housing lost at the same time, homelessness, addiction - and support to rebuild or to return home.
contacts.contact: 030 - 268 92 42 or office@barkanl.org. barkanl.org/contact lists a number per city and per language
contacts.verified_by: The office number 030 268 92 42, office@barkanl.org and the address Bernadottelaan 13, 3527 GA Utrecht are on Barka's own contact page. That page lists per-city teams with a language tag against each number - the Hague team alone publishes Polish, Bulgarian, Romanian, Russian, Turkish, Dutch and English lines - which is the basis for the languages here. Ukrainian was claimed in the previous version of this file and is NOT published by Barka, so it has been removed; what_they_do was also rewritten, because Barka's published remit is homelessness and vulnerable EU citizens rather than contract advice, and the earlier description overstated the fit.

contacts.name: Nederlandse Arbeidsinspectie (Dutch Labour Authority)
contacts.what_they_do: The government body that investigates underpayment, illegal deductions and exploitation. They can inspect an employer and impose penalties. They accept reports, including anonymous ones.
contacts.will_employer_find_out: Possibly. An inspection at your workplace may follow, and your employer will know it is happening even if your name is not given. Consider talking to a confidential organisation first about how to do this safely.
contacts.typical_response_time: Weeks to months. This is not a route to a fast answer about your own contract.
contacts.contact: 0800 - 5151, free, 24 hours a day; +31 70 333 5678 from outside the Netherlands. Report forms on nlarbeidsinspectie.nl in Dutch, English, Polish, German and Romanian
contacts.verified_by: 0800-5151, free and available 24 hours a day, and +31 70 333 5678 from abroad, are on the Arbeidsinspectie's own contact and reporting pages, which also publish report forms in Dutch, English, Polish, German and Romanian. Its Jaarverslag 2025 records that reports have been accepted in those five languages since April 2025.

contacts.name: Meld Misdaad Anoniem
contacts.what_they_do: An independent anonymous reporting line, separate from the police. Used for serious situations including forced labour and exploitation. They do not record who you are.
contacts.will_employer_find_out: They will not learn it came from you. They may learn that a report was made if an investigation follows.
contacts.typical_response_time: Unknown to you - anonymous reports are not followed up with the reporter.
contacts.contact: 0800 - 7000, Monday to Friday 08:00-22:00, weekends and public holidays 09:00-17:00. Anonymous form at meldmisdaadanoniem.nl/anoniem-melden, in English at meldmisdaadanoniem.nl/english
contacts.verified_by: 0800-7000 with those opening hours is published by Meld Misdaad Anoniem and repeated on the national police's own page about the line. English rests on the organisation's English pages and on its listing in the government's English-language trafficking guide; what language the phone line itself is answered in is not published, so the English route recorded here is the online one.
